newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-LARA COMPLETES REHABILITATION BUT WINDIES LOSE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-LARA COMPLETES REHABILITATION BUT WINDIES LOSE.

text.p: Brian Lara completed his rehabilitation with West Indies cricket on Wednesday when he captained the team for the first time but the experience ended in a crushing defeat.
West Indies lost a rain-shortened limited overs match against Western Australia at the WACA Ground by nine wickets after Lara failed with the bat.
The record-breaking left-hander led the side in the absence of veteran fast bowler Courtney Walsh, who was rested.
It was West Indies' second defeat since arriving in Perth on Saturday for a five-test series following their loss against the Chairman's XI in a low-key limited overs match on Monday.

Lara, who was fined for misconduct during last year's England tour and further angered officials by withdrawing from a subsequent limited overs tournament, was appointed vice-captain after the departure of former captain Richie Richardson.
"I like the present management. They've got a lot of faith in me," said Lara, who scored seven runs in West Indies' total of 127 for eight in 31 overs.
"I like responsiblity and in a way it helps me contribute to the side in Courtney's (Walsh) absence," he said.

The home side overhauled the total with more than 11 overs to spare, with opener Ryan Campbell unbeaten on 64 alongside Damien Martyn on 51 not out after rain reduced the game from 50 to 31 overs a side.
The two teams agreed to a second limited overs match on Thursday before the start of a three-day game on Friday.

Lara struggled to put bat to ball for 25 balls before falling to an injudicious shot outside the off stump and it was left to Jimmy Adams to guide the tourists to a respectable total with an unbeaten 48.
Campbell, who also took five catches and made one stumping, and former test batsman Martyn combined for a match-winning stand of 85 runs in just under 13 overs.
